title: SpaceX Completes History's Largest IPO, Debuts on Nasdaq at $2.1 Trillion Valuation
detail: SpaceX priced its initial public offering at $135 per share on June 11, 2026 and began trading on the Nasdaq under ticker 'SPCX' on June 12 — the largest IPO in history, raising roughly $75 billion (later $85.7 billion including the underwriters' overallotment). Shares opened at $150 and closed the first session at $161.11, up 19% from the offer price, lifting SpaceX's market capitalization to about $2.1 trillion. The IPO prospectus had framed Starlink's mission to connect the roughly 2.6 billion people still offline worldwide as central to the company's growth case, with Starlink reporting $11.39 billion in 2025 revenue and 10.3 million subscribers in Q1 2026. The listing makes SpaceX one of the most valuable publicly traded companies globally and provides fresh capital for continued Starlink constellation expansion.

title: Starlink Authorized in Côte d'Ivoire, Becomes 28th African Market
detail: The Ivorian government granted Starlink Network CIV authorization on June 12, 2026 to provide fixed satellite internet access nationwide, with commercial service set to launch in July 2026. Côte d'Ivoire becomes the 28th African market to welcome Starlink, joining a wave of 2026 approvals across the continent. The 12-month license, announced by Minister Djibril Ouattara, will be reviewed based on service quality, and targets remote rural areas, schools, and health centers currently lacking reliable internet access. The move follows Côte d'Ivoire's showcase of its 6,632 km national fiber backbone at the African Digital Week Forum in Abidjan in early June, positioning satellite and fiber as complementary tools in the country's connectivity strategy.
